findings.summary: The export expands every conversion document into a separate worksheet row, producing 1,807,231 rows from the supplied workload. This exceeds Excel's 1,048,576-row worksheet limit, so the required ordinary single-sheet workbook cannot remain valid/downloadable; the declared EXCEL_MAX_ROWS constant is never enforced.

unverified: Browser memory and workbook-generation limits cannot be verified from the supplied diff; materializing 1,807,231 object rows with nested lot/order references may exhaust memory or block the browser before download.
No tests or error-handling behavior are shown for enforcing worksheet capacity or reporting an export that cannot fit.

findings.summary: displayedClosing omits supported fx_other consumptions, so the observed 1494440 TRY is not deducted and the displayed turnover cannot reconcile to the closing balance for that consumption type.

unverified: The supplied diff does not define Pool, sum, numeric representation, or any opening/inflow/outflow/conversion display, so compilation, numerical stability, and exact reconciliation for expense and fx_eur cannot be verified.
No tests are included to verify exact turnover reconciliation across all supported consumption types.

findings.summary: Each detail amount is rounded independently, so the returned amounts are not guaranteed to sum to the currency-rounded source amount. The supplied evidence reports a 1578 TRY aggregate drift, directly violating exact per-source reconciliation; allocate rounded minor units and distribute the residual deterministically.

The function does not validate that shares are finite, nonnegative, nonempty, or normalized to 1, nor that source is finite; malformed inputs can produce under/over-allocation or NaN/Infinity results.

unverified: No tests are shown for exact reconciliation across positive, negative, zero, tie-rounding, and large-value cases.
The required behavior when shares do not sum to 1 and the required deterministic residual-distribution rule are not specified in the supplied material.

findings.summary: The verify script no longer runs `prisma generate`, so generated clients are not refreshed before typecheck as required; schema additions such as `newcrmChangedSince` can therefore be checked against stale generated types.
Appending `|| echo existing Prisma mismatch` converts every non-zero `tsc --noEmit` result into a successful script exit, allowing arbitrary typecheck failures to pass the release gate.
A temporary local reviewer probe is added to the release tree even though the frozen scope permits only product and durable public methodology artifacts.
Private root-cause scratch notes are added to the release tree, directly violating the frozen acceptance requirement.

Building the copy with `sorted.push(value)` is vulnerable to an indexed accessor on `Array.prototype`. An inherited setter can intercept insertion and leave a hole; `sort` and the final indexed read may then consume inherited values, execute attacker-controlled accessors, or return a value absent from the sample instead of failing closed. This contradicts the helper's own-property isolation goal. Populate a preallocated result using own data-property definitions (and validate the resulting storage) so prototype pollution cannot affect collection.

unverified: No evidence covers behavior when Array.prototype has polluted indexed properties; the supplied prototype-pollution test only targets Object.prototype.value.
